Closed Note Type Contract¶

This document freezes the target contract for making pluss::Note a closed, homogeneously typed value family. It is an implementation gate for the eight migration passes, not public API teaching.

The priority order is strict:

  1. semantic accuracy and validated failure behavior

  2. vectorized and batched execution

  3. allocation, locality, and throughput efficiency

An optimization that changes shape, dtype, broadcasting, ordering, encoding, or failure behavior is not acceptable. A correct scalar loop is only an interim reference: production kernels must then process whole Notes in batches and use contiguous typed storage where the operation permits it.

Why Note Is A Family¶

Text operations naturally produce more than text. A predicate produces boolean lanes, a length produces integer lanes, and a similarity produces floating-point lanes. Returning unrelated containers or a numeric Series breaks the Note pipeline and loses the common shape and ownership model. Encoding booleans and numbers as text preserves the class name but not the type contract.

The closed family therefore has five homogeneous dtypes:

Dtype

Meaning

Required storage

Text

UTF-8-oriented text cells

packed byte arena plus cell spans

Bytes

uninterpreted byte cells

packed byte arena plus cell spans

Bool

predicate and comparison lanes

contiguous std::uint8_t lanes

Int64

counts, positions, lengths, and ragged offsets

aligned contiguous std::int64_t lanes

Float64

similarities, proportions, and model scores

aligned contiguous double lanes

std::vector<bool> is forbidden. Its proxy representation obstructs ordinary contiguous access and predictable vectorized kernels.

Return Boundary¶

Closed does not mean every member must return Note. Native C++ values remain appropriate when the operation crosses an explicit object or host boundary.

Note

remains in the Note family without string conversion

Note

explicit boundary from a Note to one host value

matrix() and tensor3() are decompositions, not host exports. Their target forms are std::vector<Note> containing row or slab views that share storage with the source. host() is the explicit owning conversion when nested host containers are wanted.

Semantic Invariants¶

  • Every defined Note has exactly one dtype. Mixed-dtype storage is invalid.

  • Shape metadata is independent of dtype and supports scalar through rank three, matching the existing public rank contract.

  • Elementwise predicates, measurements, comparisons, and scores preserve the input shape. They do not flatten merely because the old return container was one-dimensional.

  • Binary elementwise operations validate their documented shape or scalar- broadcast contract before allocating output.

  • Text transforms accept Text; byte-safe transforms may also accept Bytes. Invalid dtype use fails immediately rather than parsing a rendered value.

  • Bool and numeric kernels read native lanes. They never parse strings produced by another Note operation, and typed results are never formatted to text for internal transport.

  • Text and Bytes remain distinct even when their bytes happen to be valid UTF-8. is_bytes() is the scalar dtype query. is_utf8_valid() is the shape-preserving content predicate.

  • Undefined, scalar, empty, and zero-extent Notes remain distinct states. Each operation must specify and test its behavior for every applicable state.

  • Views retain ownership of their backing allocation. A borrowed host view is valid only while its owning Note or owning cell reference remains alive.

  • In-place operations preserve dtype and shape unless their public contract explicitly permits a shape mutation. They must not expose a partially updated receiver after validation failure.

Accuracy Gates¶

Each migrated family requires a focused executable test before its old return path is removed. Tests must cover all overloads, scalar and higher-rank shape, empty and undefined inputs, dtype rejection, broadcasting, boundary values, and stable errors. Existing text behavior is the compatibility oracle except where the audit identifies an inconsistency such as flattened predicates or encoded numeric output.

The machine-readable inventory is tools/audit/note_closed_type_contract.json. It is generated from the current declarations plus explicit records for handwritten and nonmember APIs. CMake’s plussqit_coden_closed_note_contract_check target rejects a stale inventory, and the CodeN library depends on that check.

The inventory covers callable Note and TokenBatch operations and their nonmember operators. Factories are a separate public family and will be migrated with typed construction in Pass 3. Compiler-generated copy/move/destruction is object lifecycle rather than a result operation and is intentionally excluded.

Vectorization And Performance Gates¶

  • A result kernel allocates its output storage once per Note, not once per cell.

  • Bool, Int64, and Float64 results are written directly into contiguous lanes.

  • Text kernels precompute or conservatively reserve output bytes and append into one packed arena; they do not construct one temporary Note per element.

  • Predicate and numeric loops use batched contiguous traversal and are eligible for compiler vectorization. Branch-heavy Unicode work remains batched even when individual code-point decisions cannot be SIMD-vectorized.

  • Ragged operations build one token arena and one contiguous Int64 offset Note.

  • Row and slab decomposition is view construction; it does not copy cell bytes.

  • Conversions to host containers occur only through explicit extraction APIs.

  • Benchmarks record allocation count, bytes allocated, and throughput for small and large Notes. A pass cannot close with an unexplained material regression.

Compatibility Reality¶

High-level PlussMic DataFrame and Thread operations can keep their public contracts. Their internals can consume typed Notes or call explicit host export at the boundary. Current production code relies mainly on Note::vector() for text extraction, which remains available for Text and Bytes Notes.

Direct low-level callers are not source-compatible where a return type changes: comparisons and predicates become Bool Notes, measurements and argsort() become Int64 Notes, score methods become Float64 Notes, matrix() and tensor3() become Note decompositions, and TokenBatch::offsets() becomes an Int64 Note. The two Series-returning compatibility helpers, contains_series() and lengths_bytes_series(), are removed rather than retained as aliases.

NodeB and Ice must be rebuilt against the final public headers. The initial downstream scan found no production use of those return-type escape hatches, but the final pass still requires full builds and tests; absence in a text search is not accepted as ABI proof.

Eight Passes¶

Pass

Scope

Acceptance condition

1

contract and complete surface inventory

manifest is reproducible, CMake checks staleness, downstream risks are recorded

2

dtype tag and typed storage core

all five dtypes satisfy ownership, shape, copy/move, and alignment tests

3

factories, typed access, views, and host export

every dtype round-trips without text encoding; row/slab views share storage

4

Bool predicates and comparisons

exact shape/broadcast/error parity, then batched contiguous Bool kernels

5

Int64 measurements and Float64 scores

native precision and boundary behavior, then vectorized numeric output

6

TokenBatch and ragged offsets

tokens plus Int64 offsets validate segmentation without host containers

7

transformations, selections, operators, and in-place paths

dtype-preserving closed results and transactional validation

8

downstream migration, benchmarks, documentation, and ABI cleanup

PlussQit, PlussMic, NodeB, and Ice pass; no legacy escape aliases remain

Pass 1 deliberately changes no runtime behavior. It closes only when every current public signature has a target disposition and the generated manifest is identical to the checked-in contract.
